answer.rationale: The two live symptoms are onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing it plausibly moves both. Two inherited memories point here (memory_86: shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value; memory_31: cutting required signup fields lifted first-week activation), which is exactly why they are the ones worth verifying rather than trusting: they are the load-bearing claims for my chosen action, and their summaries are compressed to the point of hiding what matters. I want the original records to check (a) whether the measured lift was ever tracked past week one into paid/qualified revenue, or only to an early activation proxy, and (b) which fields were cut. That second point is the main downstream value risk: removing required signup fields degrades the qualification and routing data that feeds sales, and memory_44 says enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted path. A change that raises self-serve activation while quietly starving enterprise routing would hurt the actual objective, sustainable long-term qualified revenue, while looking like a win. memory_73 is the cautionary precedent that a headline signup/revenue lift can conceal a -12pp retention collapse that only appeared later, so I treat short-horizon lift claims as unproven on the horizon I care about. I did not pick promotional_pricing: it would match the competitor's move but memory_73 says that cohort does not retain, so it buys signups against the objective. referral_incentive (memory_57) is credible but targets established customers and does nothing for the two metrics that are actually degrading. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strong second choice and stays queued for next week if verification undercuts the onboarding records. I am running this small and guarded rather than broad because the inherited evidence is stale (days 12-52, pre-competitor-entry) and the market has changed since it was collected; a competitor taking price-sensitive SMBs may have shifted the mix of who is entering the funnel, so prior effect sizes may not transfer. Guardrails: hold enterprise/high-intent traffic out of the treatment entirely, preserve or replace any field used for sales routing, and gate on downstream qualified-revenue and retention readouts rather than declaring success on the completion-rate bump.
